title: Port E-001..E-006's acceptance checks (the 14 ledger finish bodies, 6 of them Python, and run_finish_e004_2's look assertions) to Go tests that build and drive the real program over HTTP
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived from 'HOW TO TELL IT IS DONE' 1): on a machine with no Python and no browser, `go test -count=1 ./...` passes; browser tests SKIP with a message naming CHROME_BIN; the rest run: partial
C2 (derived from 2): with CHROME_BIN set to a real browser, the browser acceptance tests run and pass, including the E-004 comment toggle and the run_finish_e004_2 look assertions: missing

C3 (derived from 3): each of E-001..E-006 has Go tests that build ./cmd/hband, start it on its own free port with a throwaway config and database and a stand-in GitHub, and talk to it only over HTTP (not internal functions): partial

C4 (derived from 4): a written mapping from every assertion in every Python file (run_finish.py, serve_show_all.py, check_e006_1_stops_at_block.py, check_run_finish_needs_chrome_bin.py, test_run_finish_edge_guard.py, .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py, and the 6 Python ledger bodies) to the Go test that now makes it: missing
C5 (derived from 5): the tests have been seen to fail when the behaviour they guard is deliberately broken, at least for a sample from each epic: missing

C6 (derived from the BROWSER RULE): browser checks go through internal/testutil/headless; the browser path comes from CHROME_BIN only; an unset or non-file CHROME_BIN skips with a message; Edge is never started; the tests read no environment and look for no browser themselves: partial

Harness package name: practice's internal/testutil/product against crossdomain's internal/testutil/program. program was chosen because E-009 line 4's own prose uses 'the product's packages' for the code under test.

Open(t), which calls Browser, against Open(tb, browser), which re-checks isEdge. Open(t) was chosen because it is structurally impossible to misuse. Crossdomain's version matched Shot's existing signature.
The E-004 browser checks as their own top-level test (practice) against subtests named 'E004 …' of one test on a shared loopback program (crossdomain).
Mapping strength: practice's one-way check of existence and count against crossdomain's two-way tag reconciliation. Two-way was chosen.
Mapping location: tests/acceptance/ported_test.go at the root package (practice), against tests/acceptance/disposition (crossdomain), against tests/acceptance/ported/ (chosen).
Tab method names: Viewport (chosen) against Emulate.
